slides.title: Welcome to the Children's Constitution Club!
slides.tip: Play welcome music.

slides.title: Roleplay Activity
body: Do you or your family follow the news?
Where do they get their news from — TV, newspapers, WhatsApp, or YouTube?
slides.tip: Remind students about the school profile if they've forgotten.

slides.title: Roleplay — The Public
body: We need 3 volunteers to play the role of the PUBLIC.
Public volunteers, please step outside the classroom. You will be called back when it's your turn!
Don't wander in the corridor! Wait right there until the teacher calls you in.
slides.tip: Select 3 volunteers and send them outside the classroom.

slides.title: Roleplay — Assign Roles
body: Today let's start with a fun activity! It's about news that different people tell in different ways.
We need 5 volunteers who can read dramatically and loudly. Who would like to participate?
Student 1: Narrator
Student 2: TV Journalist
Student 3: Local Leader
Student 4: Residents' Welfare Association & Parents
Student 5: Social Media & WhatsApp Champions
slides.tip: Give each volunteer their slip from Annexure 1.

slides.title: Roleplay — Preparation
slides.brief: The five volunteers should read their slips 2-3 times to prepare. Get ready to read a bit dramatically!
slides.tip: 1 minute preparation time.

slides.title: Roleplay — Reading Time!
body: Are the five volunteers ready to read?
Let's start in order from Student 1 to Student 4.
Student 5, wait for your turn.
Read with emotion and interest!
slides.tip: Students 1-4 read in order. Student 5 must NOT read yet.

slides.title: Invite the Public + Student 5
body: Now let's invite the public back into the classroom! Welcome back!
Now Student 5 will read the last slip, and the public must listen carefully.
slides.tip: Call the 3 public volunteers back into the classroom.

slides.title: Questions for the Public
body: The public must answer these questions:
questions: How did you feel when you heard this?
When you hear such information, what advice would you give to your loved ones?
slides.tip: Only the students playing the 'public' role should answer.

slides.title: The Narrator Reads Again
body: Now let's call the narrator back! Narrator, can you read your slip once more — this time for the public?
Did you understand what the narrator said? Was it different from what Student 5 (Social Media / WhatsApp Champion) read?
slides.tip: Ask the public: did you notice the difference between the narrator's and Student 5's versions?

slides.title: Class Discussion
body: Now that you have heard all versions of the news, let's discuss together:
What happened in this example?
Why did the original news change depending on who was telling it?
What are the consequences of spreading fake news or giving wrong information?
Did you believe everything immediately? Did you pause and think?
Did you ask questions or compare what different people said?
slides.tip: If heated debate arises: 'Many people feel this way, but let's calmly hear other views too.' If students argue or interrupt: 'We cannot all speak at once. When someone is sharing, please be patient and listen. Then you can give your response.' Let students reach conclusions themselves.

slides.title: Roleplay — Scientific Temper
body: When we ask questions, verify facts, and think clearly before believing or forwarding something — we are using something very important.
Can you guess what it's called?
slides.tip: MC video Part 1 needed (not yet produced). Wait 5 seconds for the answer.

slides.title: Scientific Temper
prompts: Have you heard this word before?
Meaning: Using your brain like a detective — asking for evidence, staying calm, and accepting the truth without being swayed by emotions.
This is how we fight fake news and misinformation — by thinking like scientists and asking questions!
slides.tip: MC video Part 2 needed (not yet produced).

slides.title: 4Ws Test
slides.intro: When reading any news, can you guess what these 4 words might mean?
prompts: WHO — Who is saying this? News channels, officials, etc.
WHAT — What is my current opinion about this? Did I just accept this news as-is?
WHERE — Where can I cross-check this information? Internet, different news channels, newspapers, government websites.
WHETHER — Am I willing to change my old opinions based on new evidence?
slides.tip: Let students guess first, then reveal each answer.

slides.title: What are the 4Ws?
body: The 4Ws is an extremely useful and important tool to determine whether the news or information you receive is true or false!
slides.tip: Write 4Ws on the board: WHO, WHAT, WHERE, WHETHER.

slides.title: Social Media Post
body: Let's read a social media post and use the 4Ws test! Would any volunteer like to come up and read this?
BREAKING NEWS: Government bans online transactions nationwide!

Citing rising cybersecurity threats, the Indian government has reportedly decided to ban all types of online payments from next month. According to a leaked government notification circulating on social media, popular platforms such as UPI, net banking, and digital wallets will be completely shut down to protect citizens from increasing cyber fraud. The directive has warned businesses and individuals to prepare for cash-based transactions, causing widespread concern among those dependent on the digital economy.

Economic experts have expressed concern that the sudden decision could cripple businesses that depend on digital payments, while citizens are rushing to ATMs and banks to withdraw money. Several e-commerce websites have reportedly started changing their payment systems, while fintech companies are trying to get clarity from government sources.

This post talks about banning online transactions including UPI services. It has been shared by many popular social media influencers and is circulating in WhatsApp forwards, Twitter posts, and Facebook discussions!
slides.tip: Ask a volunteer to read the post aloud.

slides.title: 4Ws Test — WHAT & WHO
slides.intro: Do you have a favourite social media influencer? Imagine they have posted that online transactions including UPI services have been banned. You believe it and share it without verifying whether it is true. Let's use the 4Ws test!
prompts: WHAT — What are my current opinions about this social media post? If the influencer who shared this post is someone you like, what happens? Does it change your reaction or not? → It's important to notice our current opinions and preferences about information that comes to us on social media, because this can shape our positions.

WHO — Who spread this news? Social media, influencers. But who are these social media influencers? What reason is there to trust them? Are they reliable just because they have likes and followers? → Not necessarily!
slides.tip: Reveal each answer on click.

slides.title: 4Ws Test — WHETHER & WHERE
slides.intro: The remaining part of the 4Ws test:
prompts: WHETHER — Am I willing to change my old opinions based on new evidence? Even if you have believed and shared something, if someone shows you a reliable source proving it is wrong, would you change your decision? → We must be ready to change our decisions based on evidence!

WHERE — Where can we cross-check this information? Which sources are more reliable? Who knows more about economics, banking, finance, etc.? → Other newspapers, independent sources, RBI and government websites, answers given in Parliament, reported cybercrime data. Find out what the experts are saying!
slides.tip: Reveal each answer on click.

slides.title: AI and Fake News
body: It is very important to always stop and check before believing or sharing anything.
AI (Artificial Intelligence) can also create images, videos, and news that deceive people! This creates even more fake news and spreads misinformation.
slides.tip: AI-generated news example image needed (not yet ready).

slides.title: Constitution and Scientific Temper
body: Which constitutional value from the Preamble best fits the activities and discussions we did today?
Share with your teacher.
slides.tip: Show Preamble image. Accept all responses.

slides.title: Fundamental Duty
body: Our Constitution guarantees us rights. There is a Fundamental Duty in the Indian Constitution about verifying the truth of what we read, hear, and speak, and thinking critically.
Can you guess what this Fundamental Duty actually says?
Yes! It is: to develop scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
Did you know that applying the 4Ws test is part of our Fundamental Duty?
slides.tip: MC video needed (not yet produced).

slides.title: Ripple Task
body: With your parents' permission, check some forwarded messages on their mobile phones when you go home and apply the 4Ws test to verify the information.
Do not use their phones without their permission.
Discuss with your parents and share this fun activity you did about forward messages or online news!
I will distribute handouts to everyone. These will be very helpful for you to verify information and data.
Your activities will be considered Ripples of Change and can be added to your Club's Box.
slides.tip: Teachers must distribute Annexure 3 (4Ws handout) to all students.
